title: Exodus Bible Quiz - Chapter 27
description: Ten questions on Exodus 27: the bronze altar, the court of the tabernacle and the oil for the lamp.

questions.text: What shape was the altar to have?
questions.explanation: The altar was to be five cubits long and five cubits wide; the altar was to be square.

answers.text: Twice as long as it was wide

questions.text: What was to be made on the four corners of the altar?
questions.explanation: Horns were to be made on its four corners, of one piece with the altar.

questions.text: What metal was the altar overlaid with?
questions.explanation: The altar of acacia wood was to be overlaid with bronze, and all its vessels made of bronze.

questions.text: How far up the altar was the bronze net to reach?
questions.explanation: The grating was put under the ledge around the altar, so that the net would reach halfway up the altar.

questions.text: How was the altar to be made?
questions.explanation: The altar was to be made hollow with planks, as it had been shown on the mountain.

questions.text: How long were the hangings for the south side of the court?
questions.explanation: The hangings of fine twined linen for the south side were to be one hundred cubits long.

questions.text: What were the hooks and fillets of the court's pillars made of?
questions.explanation: The hooks of the pillars and their fillets were to be of silver, while their sockets were bronze.

questions.text: How wide was the screen for the gate of the court?
questions.explanation: The gate of the court was to have a screen of twenty cubits, the work of the embroiderer.

questions.text: What were the Israelites to bring for the light?
questions.explanation: They were to bring pure olive oil beaten for the light, to cause a lamp to burn continually.

answers.text: Pure olive oil beaten for the light
Oil mixed with sweet spices and myrrh

questions.text: Who was to keep the lamp in order from evening to morning?
questions.explanation: In the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil, Aaron and his sons were to keep it in order from evening to morning before Yahweh.
